title: Predator-Prey Population Dynamics
description: Watch predator and prey populations oscillate out of phase in an animated Lotka-Volterra meadow.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Systems Thinking Across Disciplines

educational.learningObjective: Given the animated predator and prey populations, the learner will explain why the two populations oscillate out of phase over time in a balancing feedback system.
prerequisites: Knows what a balancing loop is
learningOutcomes: Explain why the two populations oscillate out of phase
Identify the feedback delay that produces the phase lag
Recognize the same delay-driven oscillation in non-ecological systems
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Show a phase-lagged pair of curves and ask learners to identify which is the predator and to justify the answer from the lag.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Animated agent simulation with paired population time-series
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Structural analogy back to the delay concept from Chapter 6
pedagogical.feedbackType: Live meadow animation plus two synchronized population graphs
misconceptionsAddressed: That a balancing loop always settles at a steady value
That the two populations peak together
discussionQuestions: Why does this balancing loop oscillate rather than settle?
What is the predator-prey equivalent in a hiring market, or in inventory management?
